messages:
Maya: FYI I merged the customer's Quietus LoRA into the 1.4-serving branch and kicked off the quick-eval pack. Seeing an embedding-scale shift when quantizing to int4 — amount parsing accuracy dropped ~6%. :eyes:
Raj: Can you paste the numbers and the eval command you ran?
Maya: Ran: ```./scripts/run_eval.sh --model quietus-lora-merge --quant int4 --suite invoice-parsing --mirror s3://evals/quietus/tmp```
Maya: Quick output (trimmed):
```
BLEU: 31.2 -> 30.9 (-0.3)
ExactMatch: 78.1 -> 76.5 (-1.6)
amount_parsing_accuracy: 92.4% -> 86.3% (-6.1)
median_latency_ms: 48 -> 46
```
Raj: 6% on amount parsing is pretty visible. Any tokenization diffs between base and LoRA?
Claire: Could be embedding scale / prefix KV mismatch after quant. We've seen money-formatting be sensitive to small vector shifts. Did you run tokenizer round-trips?
Maya: Not yet. I did a quick spot check and noticed some tokens collapsing around currency symbols. Example: "$\u00a0" vs "$" mapped differently in the merged tokenizer mapping table.
Jon: Two quick mitigations: (1) try int8 quant for routes handling financial parsing, (2) apply a rescale to the merged LoRA embedding output (empirically 0.98 helped in prior case).
Sofia: Customer success heads-up: if this affects production routes we should canary and maybe fallback to dedicated int8. I'll loop in the AE if we see regression in their traffic. :exclamation:
ci-bot: smoke-eval queued (id: smoke-7490012345-1) — running unit/invoice-parsing on quietus-lora-merge int4.
Maya: I pushed a quick patch that rescales LoRA out vector by 0.985 in the merge script: commit 9f3b2c4. Re-running smoke: ```./scripts/run_eval.sh --model quietus-lora-merge-rescale0.985 --quant int4 --suite invoice-parsing```
Maya: New quick output (trimmed):
```
amount_parsing_accuracy: 92.1% -> 90.8% (-1.3)
BLEU: 31.2 -> 31.0 (-0.2)
ExactMatch: 78.1 -> 77.4 (-0.7)
```
Raj: Nice — rescale helped a lot. Still a small delta but acceptable for a canary. Let's also run the full quickpack (all suites) on a small sample and compare int8 baseline.
Claire: Also add a tokenizer sanity check to the eval pack: roundtrip tokenization + numeric normalization test. If that passes we can be confident the fix addresses both mapping and scale.
Jon: I'll prepare a routing policy that sends 5% traffic to int4 rescaled, 95% to int8 baseline for the customer if we need fast rollback.
Sofia: Sounds good. I'll tell the AE the plan + rollback path.
Maya: Assigning follow-up actions: I own the full quickpack run and will upload detailed logs to s3://evals/quietus/7490012345/; will open a short ticket with the diff and recommended merge flag (rescale or prefer-int8).
Raj: Thanks — please post smoke run id when full quickpack finishes. (reaction :thumbsup:)
ci-bot: smoke-eval completed (id: smoke-7490012345-1) — summary uploaded to s3://evals/quietus/7490012345/summary.json.
Maya: Posted summary link and will draft the canary plan. Closing thread unless we see any more regressions. (reaction :white_check_mark:)
